title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 73
paragraphs: Of the Athenians, the man who gained most glory is said to have been Sophanes son of Eutychides of the deme of Dekeleia — a deme whose inhabitants long ago performed a deed that has been of service to them ever since, as the Athenians themselves report. For when, in olden times, the sons of Tyndareus invaded Attica with a great army to bring back Helen, and were laying waste the demes — not knowing to what hiding place Helen had been taken — then they say that the men of Dekeleia (or, as some say, Dekelos himself), aggrieved by the insolence of Theseus and fearing for the whole land of the Athenians, told them the whole matter and led them to Aphidnai, which Titakos, a man sprung from the soil, delivered up by treachery to the sons of Tyndareus. As a result of this deed, the Dekeleians have continued to enjoy freedom from dues at Sparta and front seats at the games — privileges still in effect to this day. Indeed, in the war which arose many years after these events between the Athenians and Peloponnesians, when the Lacedaemonians laid waste all the rest of Attica, they spared Dekeleia from harm.
